answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks via hardware remote attestation. An isolated enclave kernel cryptographically signs the agent binary, publishing valid measurements to a decentralized Merkle grove. Binding identity keys to silicon sealed in tamper-evident onyx packaging forces attackers to buy dedicated chips per agent instead of cheap software clones. However, microarchitectural side-channel leaks can compromise root keys, allowing adversaries to forge attestations.
